name: Bimetric-Split Slip MOND (BSS-MOND)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture abandons the single-metric constraint, utilizing Hassan-Rosen bimetric gravity where the interaction mass m provides an independent, finite kinetic normalization for the scalar sector. The scalar phi couples to the massive spin-2 mode, generating a non-conformal slip (eta != 1) that satisfies the DC-013 requirement for off-ray lensing without a propagating preferred-frame vector. The preferred-frame coupling is screened by e^-y, ensuring Solar System PPN compliance, while the slip is dynamically generated by the bimetric mass term rather than a screened longitudinal mode, thereby evading the P7 strong-coupling wall.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the bimetric interaction yields a scalar-mediated slip (eta ~ 1 + O(m^2/|k|^2)) that breaks the diff-invariance lock, allowing for MOND-enhanced lensing (Psi != Phi). The preferred-frame coupling to acceleration is suppressed by e^-y, vanishing in the Solar System and restoring GR. The massive spin-2 mode decays at scales below 1/m, leaving a local scalar-tensor theory in the sub-Compton regime.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is fundamentally inequivalent to DC-001, DC-010, DC-013, and DC-014 because it operates outside the single-metric class. The slip is generated by the bimetric mass term (independent of the screened coupling), directly resolving the P7 collision where the screened coupling and kinetic normalization were previously locked together. Unlike DC-013, it is not subject to the frame-free slip-lock theorem because it contains an explicit preferred-frame coupling (albeit screened). Unlike DC-010/DC-014, the kinetic normalization of the propagating scalar is set by the bimetric mass, not the screened e^-y factor, avoiding the strong-coupling divergence.
